div.head: Forf 1
div.ab: Forfang ubique, sit in una scyre, sit in pluribus, XV den. (sint); et de omni paruo pecore semper pro solido denarius reddatur.
Forfang ofer eall, sy hit on anre sci[r]e, sy hit on má, fiftyne peningas; ⁊ æt ælcon smalon orfe æfre æt scyll' penig.
Forfang ofer eal, sy hit on an scire, sy hit on má, fiftyne penegas; 7 ælcon smalon orfe æfre æt scillinge peni.

[The reward for] the seizure/recovery [of stolen property] is [to be the same] everywhere, be it in one shire, be it in [over] several: 15 pence; and for every small animal a penny shall always be paid per shilling [of the value of the property].

[Lohn für] Ergreifung [gestohlenen Viehs] überall, sei es in Einer Grafschaft [derselben, wo es gestohlen war, eingefangen], sei es über mehrere hin, [beträgt] 15 Pfennig; und von jedem kleinen Vieh [zahle Eigenthümer dem Retter] je vom Schilling [Werth: 1] Pfennig.

[The reward for] seizing [stolen cattle] everywhere, whether in one shire [the same one where it was stolen] or across several, [is] 15 pence; and for each small beast [let the owner pay the rescuer] one penny per shilling [of value].

div.note: The Latin is the Quadripartitus; Liebermann's Old English is from H (Textus Roffensis f. 32, after Blaseras without a break, c. 1120), and B (p. 1) is also given here. H reads ‘scipe’; Liebermann prints ‘sci[r]e’. B lacks ‘æt’ before ‘ælcon’. Liebermann dates Forfang c. 900–c. 1000, perhaps c. 960. In H, Ordal follows after a paragraph break. Liebermann compares Forf 2.
